summary_rationale: Texas Instruments operates one of the highest-quality franchises in global semiconductors: an ~80,000-product Analog and Embedded Processing catalog serving 100,000+ customers across Industrial (33%), Automotive (33%), Personal Electronics (21%), and Data Center (9%), with >80% direct channel reach via TI.com. Its 300mm wafer fab buildout (RFAB1/RFAB2, LFAB1/LFAB2, SM1/SM2) creates a durable ~40% die-cost advantage over 200mm peers and targets >95% internal wafer output by 2030. After the 2023–2024 destocking downturn and $14.44B three-year capex wave, 2026 inflected sharply: Q3 2026 revenue grew 28% YoY to $6.06B (Q4 guided $5.80B–$6.30B), gross margin jumped to 64.2%, capex stepped down toward $2B–$3B, and TTM FCF reached $8.42B (~$6.85B ex-$1.57B CHIPS cash, aided by the July 2025 OBBBA raising the Section 48D ITC from 25% to 35%). Key watch items surfaced in forensic audit: (1) single-customer concentration (one unnamed Analog buyer at 12% of FY2024–FY2025 revenue); (2) China trade exposure (23% of Q3 2026 revenue from China-HQ buyers and ~50% of 2025 shipments entering China, plus $499M regulatory reverse break fee on Silicon Labs, which derives 30.9% of sales in China); (3) pro-forma debt principal rising from $13.65B to $15.65B following the Nov 9, 2026 $2.0B senior notes issue ($10.13B pro-forma cash, 101% Special Mandatory Redemption clause, $5B delayed-draw term loan); and (4) elevated inventory at 194 days ($4.67B).
